title: Recover a MUX-based ALU Datapath's Word-Level Function
description: Given a flattened, obfuscated gate-level netlist of a small combinational ALU-style datapath (two 8-bit operands, a 2-bit select, one 8-bit output), reverse-engineer and reconstruct a clean word-level Verilog module that is functionally equivalent to the reference netlist for every input combination.
expected_output_summary: A single Verilog file at submission/recovered_rtl.v defining exactly one module named recovered_datapath with the pinned port list (a[7:0], b[7:0], sel[1:0], y[7:0]), purely combinational, that reproduces the reference gate_netlist.v output exactly across a broad randomized and directed simulation sweep of (a,b,sel) vectors.

metrics.name: word_recovery_rate
metrics.description: Fraction of the 4 opcode operations (add, sub, and, or) correctly identified and implemented, measured via per-opcode simulation pass/fail.

metrics.name: structural_match_accuracy
metrics.description: Degree to which the recovered module's port list and combinational structure conform to the pinned interface (module name, port widths, purely combinational).

metrics.name: functional_equivalence
metrics.description: Percentage of randomized+directed (a,b,sel) test vectors for which recovered_datapath output matches the reference gate_netlist.v output exactly, via iverilog/vvp simulation.

constraints: The submission must not modify any file under inputs/.
The recovered_datapath module must be purely combinational (no clocked always blocks, no latches).
The design must not instantiate or depend on any vendor-specific primitives; only standard Verilog constructs are allowed.
The output y must be driven for every combination of sel.
